title.narrative: Rebuilding Lives: Integrated Humanitarian Support for Returning IDPs in Horo Guduru Wollega zone, Abe Dongoro district

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe proposed project delivers integrated, time-bound humanitarian assistance to returning IDPs and conflict-affected populations in Abe Dongoro district, Horo Guduru Wollega Zone, addressing urgent needs in Agriculture, MPCA, ES/NFI, GBV, Health, and WASH. The protracted crisis has led to food insecurity, livelihood collapse, displacement, and protection risks, including SGBV and weakened social systems. Women, girls, and vulnerable groups face heightened risks of sexual violence, child marriage, and exploitation.nbspThrough a multisectoral, community-centered approach, the project will restore livelihoods, improve food security, strengthen protection mechanisms, and enhance access to essential services, reducing dependence on external aid.nbspThe Agriculture and Livelihoods component targets 13,167 people (6633 females) through the provision of crop seeds, farm tools, and cash support to resume cultivation and stabilize food security.nbspThe MPCA intervention supports 550 female-headed households through unconditional cash transfers to meet urgent food and shelter needs, prevent negative coping mechanisms, uphold dignity, and stimulate local markets.nbspThe ES/NFI response benefits 1,304 people (653 females) with emergency shelter kits and repair cash, ensuring safe, dignified living conditions and reducing protection and health risks.nbspThe GBV response reaches 620 women and girls through case management, psychosocial support, legal aid, and referrals. Dignity kits and community awareness campaigns will promote hygiene, safety, and behavioral change, while engaging schools, religious leaders, and communities to address harmful gender norms and strengthen local prevention systems.nbspThe Health component targets 16,570 people (8,310 females) via Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs), providing primary healthcare, maternal and child health services, immunization, and MHPSS, with strong referral linkages.nbspThe WASH component supports 8,000 individuals (4,000 females) through rehabilitation of water points, hygiene promotion, and hygiene kit distribution, improving access to safe water and sanitation and reducing disease risks.nbspImplementation follows a participatory, community-driven approach, leveraging SOS Sahel Ethiopia’s technical expertise and partnerships with local authorities, community structures, and line offices for coordinated delivery and local ownership.nbspCapacity-building for service providers, community leaders, and protection committees will enhance coordination, strengthen referral pathways, and ensure sustainability beyond the project’s duration.nbspIn total, the project will directly benefit 40209 people (20,491 females) and indirectly benefit 44,740 others through improved services, awareness, and protection mechanisms.nbspOver nine months, with a total budget of USD 400,000 funded by the Ethiopia Humanitarian Fund (EHF), the project will restore livelihoods, enhance food security, strengthen protection, and rebuild resilience in Abe Dongoro addressing interconnected needs through an integrated humanitarian response. The project will enable returnees and vulnerable households to rebuild their lives safely, restore dignity, and strengthen resilience against future shocks.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
